raw_text:
Become a Bar Raiser - The Quintessential Talent Ambassador
Philips Intranet, Chief Technology Office
Author: Ramchandran, Prabha, Digital TA Consultant Asia, India Digital, Q&R, R&D
Published: September 25th 2020

Organizations thrive on great people, and people thrive in great organizations. What makes one a prized employee? Resourcefulness, being a 'Role Model' to others, having an appetite to take calculated risk and a 'Not afraid to fail' attitude. Similarly, a prized organization is one, which can attract and retain such employees. The U.S. Department of Labor estimates that a bad hire can cost an organization up to 30% of the employee's potential first-year expected earnings. Hence, it is very critical to attract the right talent.

Amazon started its Bar Keeper program in 1999 by creating a group of interviewers, who could identify the right set of candidates that fit the organization's culture and leadership parameters. Because the purpose of the program was to raise the standard with every new hire and not maintain it, the Bar Keepers eventually became the Bar Raisers. This meant that candidates selected by the Bar Raiser had to be better than 50% of those performing similar roles in the organization.

In Philips, with our focus changing from healthcare to healthtech, Talent Acquisition, in association with the Software Center of Excellence, embarked on a similar journey in 2020. They have piloted the first Philips Bar Raiser Program with a 10-member team in Philips Innovation Campus in Bangalore. This was part of adopting best practices in the technology space and strengthening our focus on the 'Workforce of the Future'. After initiation, TA has successfully replicated the program across the US, EMEA and Blumenau.

The 10 Bar Raisers from Philips Innovation Campus Bangalore: Anasuya Mohan Rao, Sundaresan Jagadeesan, Dattatreya Vellal, Karthick Ramanathan, Nikila Gangadharan, Suyog Gaidhani, Prasad Thakar, Sankara N Balasubramanian, Minatee Mishra, Rajesh Arasu.

Journey so far and the milestones:

Milestone One: Initiation: One of the most critical and time-intensive phases was identifying the Bar Raisers. These individuals lead by examples, are very passionate about people and always go an extra mile to engage with the candidates. They are the influencers and the 'go to' persons in any team. Simao William from the Software Center of Excellence also personally addressed the team and brought in his insights. Their work emulates our five behaviors, which constantly takes us closer to our mission.

Milestone Two: Preparation: The identified Bar Raisers had to go through a mandatory training session to understand the assessment and the evaluation process - STARR. This process focusses on drawing concrete examples from past behaviors, instead of predicting future actions. The training session helped the Bar Raisers prepare for a structured interview and provide feedback with substantial data. It also advocated the importance of a debrief session with all the interviewers in the hiring process.

Milestone Three: Experimentation: The team has conducted over more than 40 Bar Raiser interviews so far and the learning has been immense. Both candidates and hiring managers have expressed the value this particular round brings to the entire selection process. Candidates feel more vested and hiring managers get a very neutral and unbiased perspective.

Testimonials:
- 'The program is my Ikigai, it aligns with my personal mission and helps me contribute towards building my organization's capability, provide deeper insights and enhance candidate experience' – Anasuya Rao Mohan, PIC Bar Raiser
- 'It was great speaking to Suyog Gaidhani (PIC, Bar Raiser). I could feel the intensity of the questions to understand true motivation, passion, skills and most importantly my ambition. With this conversation, I am more interested in the opportunity with Philips' – A potential hire
- 'Dear Datta, Very descriptive and detailed feedback. Really, appreciate this. I am seeing great value in having a Bar raisers interview round' – Hiring Manager, PIC

The program has led to an enormous cross-pollination of ideas, gaining insights into other businesses and most importantly, our Bar Raisers have become the quintessential ambassadors of our hiring process. The team meets every month to share experiences and learn from each other.

This has been our story so far from the India Bar Raiser Chapter; we will come back with the other stories from EMEA, US and Blumenau in our future editions.

raw_text:
End-to-End Software Development & Operations
The role of DevOps, a common CI-CD pipeline, Platforms and Hosting & Operations and how it all fits together
April 2021 — A CAO whitepaper
Doc ID: CAO_2021_42 | Version: 1.0 | Status: Final | Classification: For Internal Use

Authors:
- Herwig Wens, Fellow Architect, Chief Architect Office
- Rajesh Arasu, Principal Architect, PIC
- Dattatreya Vellal, Competency Specialist, SWCoE
- Niek Palm, Sr. Architect, SWAT EIH
- Gert Jan Kamstra, Sr. Software Architect, SWAT EIH
- Marco Franssen, Sr. Software Architect, SWAT EIH
- Nagaraj Shamanna, I2M TA, PIC

Reviewers: Jan Van Zoest (Chief Architect), Simao Williams (Head of Competencies Software COE), Eran Rubens (Head of AD & Informatics Strategy), Klaas Wijbrans (Fellow Architect, CAO), Nico Van Rooijen (Fellow Architect, CAO), Stef Zaiscek (CAO Portfolio Manager), Ck Andrade (CAO r Director, Digital Product Management & Marketing), Ke Ke Qi (Principal Architect, CDI), Cluster Architects, Rani Mali (sr. Dir SWCoE), Ralph Holdorp (Department Head Software Concepts), Hugo Biemans (sr. Dir, IT I2M TA, IT for R&D)

Objective:
1. Paint the bigger picture of End-2-End Software Development and Operations at Philips including DevOps and Hosting & Operations into context of HealthSuite Reference Architecture and Platforms, and the benefits it brings to the Solutions and Services. Sketch the North Star for alignment and direction.
2. Dive deeper into DevOps and define a standardized way of working with respect to Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD) within Philips.

Scope: Product software development and operations at Philips (excluding embedded software).

Six Pillars for End-to-End Software Delivery:
1. PILLAR 1: HealthSuite Reference Architecture (HSRA) — Guardrails for software architecture alignment
2. PILLAR 2: HealthSuite Platforms — Platform services and capabilities
3. PILLAR 3: Modularization and Microservices — Breaking down monoliths, modular architecture
4. PILLAR 4: (Biz)Dev(Sec)Ops by means of CI/CD — Three principles: Flow, Feedback, Continual Learning & Experimentation. From DevOps to DevSecOps to BizDevOps. Capability view of DevOps. Metrics (DORA metrics).
5. PILLAR 5: Central Hosting & Operations — Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Hosting & Operations
6. PILLAR 6: An Agile way of working with SAFe

CI/CD Pipeline Reference Architecture:
- Guiding principles for Philips E2E CI/CD Pipeline: seamlessly integrated in E2E value chain with E2E visibility
- The CI/CD reference pipeline
- The NorthStar minimal standard toolset of the CI/CD reference pipeline
- Extending and adapting the CI/CD reference pipeline
- Practicing Shift Left

CI/CD Use Cases:
- Diagnostic Imaging (DI)
- TASY
- IntelliSpace Enterprise Edition (ISEE)
- External examples: DevOps at Microsoft (moving 65000 engineers to cloud-based DevOps), DevOps at MS Universal Store, DevOps at Capital One (Clean Room principle)

The Bigger Picture of End-to-End DevOps at Philips
CI/CD Pipeline Reference Architecture (detailed)
The Journey to Our NorthStar

Problem Statement: How do we prevent chaos in having a lot of developers and teams contributing software to a Solution when we will do this at scale? How do we make sure the different building blocks are easy to assemble to compose a solution with the right quality and speed and assets are reused? How can we easily distinguish between regulated and non-regulated parts of the product and solution? How do we make sure things do not break in the next release? How do we make sure Customers have always the latest and greatest update? How do we assure that when things break, we can deliver a fix as soon as possible, preferably before the Customer notices? How do we collect the right operational and customer feedback data and use it correctly?
